question: How do I reliably page Stellar RPC getTransactions and getEvents with the cursor, and detect when my poller falls behind the per-call 200 limit?

golden.answer: For the first `getTransactions` page send an inclusive `startLedger` and optional `limit`; afterward omit `startLedger` and send the response's opaque `pagination.cursor`, which resumes after the last item. The two are mutually exclusive. Persist the new cursor only after downstream writes succeed. As of 2026-11-14 stock stellar-rpc defaults `getTransactions` to 50 with a maximum of 200, `getEvents` to 100/10000 and `getLedgers` to 50/200; these are operator-configurable options, so providers can differ. Horizon is 10 default, 200 max. A cursor cannot recover history outside retention, so a poller that falls behind needs an indexer or data lake. RPC returns failed as well as successful transactions.
keyFacts: First page uses an inclusive startLedger; later pages use the opaque cursor alone.
Stock limits, dated: getTransactions 50/200, getEvents 100/10000, getLedgers 50/200.
These are configurable defaults that providers can change, not protocol constants.
A cursor cannot recover history beyond retention; falling behind needs an indexer or lake.
avoid: Do NOT repeat startLedger with a cursor, edit the cursor or treat it as a ledger number.
Do NOT claim the 200 limit is Horizon-only or that RPC has no 200-record cap.
Do NOT claim the stock 50/200 is immutable for every provider.
golden.notes: Canonical-page caution: the official getTransactions page calls the cap hardcoded. An attributed quote of that page is not a wrong claim while improvements/stellar-docs/sd-004-rpc-limits-described-as-hardcoded.md stays declined-upstream; grade caps at partial. This does not accept universal immutability. Either the documented stock 50/200 or a dated source-level configurable-default qualifier is correct.
